definitions.gloss: facing each other; sitting opposite; face to face
definitions.explanation: A seating or spatial arrangement where two people or things are positioned directly across from each other.

examples.japanese: {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせに{座|すわ}った。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{向|む}かい{合|あ}わせの{席|せき}は{少|すこ}し{気|き}まずい。
examples.english: The facing seats on the train are a little awkward.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}はテーブルを{挟|はさ}んで{向|む}かい{合|あ}わせに{座|すわ}り、{静|しず}かに{話|はな}し{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The two sat across from each other at the table and quietly began to talk.

notes:
Describes a spatial arrangement where two things or people directly face one another. Most commonly used for seating arrangements on trains, at tables, or in waiting rooms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせに{座|すわ}る: to sit facing each other
- {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせの{席|せき}: facing seats
- {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせの{家|いえ}: the house directly opposite
- {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせに{並|なら}べる: to arrange facing each other

USAGE:
Typically used as an adverbial phrase with に ({向|む}かい{合|あ}わせに) or as a noun modifier with の ({向|む}かい{合|あ}わせの{席|せき}). On Japanese trains, some cars have {向|む}かい{合|あ}わせ seating (box seats facing each other) while others have forward-facing rows.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {向|む}かい: across the way, opposite (refers to a location across from you)
- {対面|たいめん}: face-to-face meeting or encounter (emphasizes the act of meeting rather than the spatial arrangement)
- {正面|しょうめん}: the front; directly in front of something
